newsitem.title: UK: Blue Circle cement unit signs 3 yr pay deal.
newsitem.headline: Blue Circle cement unit signs 3 yr pay deal.

text.p: Britain's Blue Circle Industries Plc's cement manufacturing division said on Monday it had signed a long-term pay deal with its 2,000 employees and their four trade unions.
The deal, outlined in January, gives the bulk of its employees a three-year deal of inflation plus 0.25 percent in return for employment security.
The deal will realise 10 million stg in annualised savings, the company said in a statement.

After being flagged earlier in the year, the pay deal has been agreed between Blue Circle Cement and the GMB, Transport and General, Amalgamated Engineering and Electrical Union and the British Cement Staff Association trade unions.
The company said the deal would bring "improved business efficiency and productivity in return for guaranteed pay rises and employment security".
The deal follows a wide internal review and means there will be no barrier to reorganisation or restructuring within BCC. There will also be an ongoing voluntary redundancy programme.
This latest pay deal follows a similar arrangement reached with 127 lorry drivers earlier in the year. It also harmonises employment terms for different types of workers.
BCC will seek to roll out the pay deal beyond its initial three-year term and has undertaken to work towards a 37-hour week by 2001.

Ian McKenzie, BCC chief executive, said "We are very pleased to have reached this agreement which will improve further the competitive position of BCC and help secure the future of our UK cement operations and of employment in the long-term."
